title: Breach Predictor portal: licensing, ZIA prerequisite, sign-in, profile and theme

license.statement: Breach Predictor is a standalone product that is licensed separately from other parts of the Zscaler ecosystem.

quotes: Zscaler Breach Predictor is a standalone product that is licensed separately from other parts of the Zscaler ecosystem.

zia-prereq.statement: For ZIA logs to be available to Breach Predictor, ZIA must be fully configured; an organization that already uses ZIA needs no extra configuration for Breach Predictor to access ZIA logs.

quotes: To ensure that Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) logs are available for Breach Predictor, ZIA must be fully configured for your organization.
If your organization already uses ZIA, no extra configuration is required for Breach Predictor to access ZIA logs.

signin-methods.statement: Portal sign-in goes through the Authentication Service, using the method set by the organization's authentication preference: Password, Email One-Time Password (OTP), or Security Key or Biometric; the Breach Predictor tile then opens the portal.

quotes: Based on your organization's authentication preference, sign in to Authentication Service using one of the following methods:
- Password
- Email One-Time Password (OTP)
- Security Key or Biometric
Click the Breach Predictor tile to access the Breach Predictor Portal.

mfa.statement: In the Password sign-in steps, after the password is entered, whether 2FA is required depends on the organization's MFA policy.

quotes: Enter your password and click Sign In.
Based on your organization's MFA policy, 2FA is required.

email-otp.statement: An email OTP sign-in is available to accounts configured with MFA; the OTP expires after 15 minutes, and Resend issues another OTP after 60 seconds.

quotes: If your account is configured with MFA, you can sign in using an email OTP:
The OTP expires after 15 minutes. If the OTP expires or you don't receive an OTP, click Resend to receive another OTP after 60 seconds.

reset-links.statement: From Having trouble signing in?, Reset Password, Reset Second Factor and Reset Security Key or Biometric each send a reset link to the user's email, and the link expires after 15 minutes.

quotes: click Having trouble signing in? > Reset Password or Reset Second Factor, and a reset link is sent to your email ID. The reset link expires after 15 minutes.
click Having trouble signing in? > Reset Security Key or Biometric, and a reset link is sent to your email ID. The reset link expires after 15 minutes.

profile-contents.statement: Profile shows the username, license, the Zscaler cloud Breach Predictor is connected to, the organization ID of the organization's ZIA instance, and the available integrations (for example Jira, CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM and Splunk).

quotes: Click Profile to see basic information about your username, your license, the Zscaler cloud to which Breach Predictor is connected, and the organization ID for your organization's instance of Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA).
Additionally, you can see the various integrations available in your organization (e.g., Jira, CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM, and Splunk).

profile-tabs.statement: The My Profile page has a User Detail tab (basic user and organizational information) and an Integration tab (the applications available for integration, which can be configured there).

quotes: On the User Detail tab, you can do the following:
See basic user and organizational information.
On the Integration tab, you can do the following:
See which applications are available for integration with Breach Predictor and configure them.

theme.statement: A Theme toggle in the navigation sets the UI to dark mode or light mode.

quotes: To specify the UI theme (i.e., dark mode or light mode), click the Theme toggle.

no-config-upgrades.statement: Under Understanding Maintenance and Upgrades, the navigation page says Breach Predictor does not require configuration for new data visibility (for example new logs or data sources), so an organization automatically benefits from added functionality; release notes track enhancements.

quotes: Understanding Maintenance and Upgrades
Breach Predictor doesn’t require configuration for new data visibility (e.g., new logs, data sources, etc.), your organization automatically benefits from added functionality.
You can stay up to date with Breach Predictor enhancements by tracking release notes updates.
